welcome.intro: See the energy use of your home, live and back in time.
welcome.label: EMON ID
welcome.helpTitle: Where do I find my EMON ID?
welcome.helpText: You saw your EMON ID when you set up the meter kit through the Wi-Fi network "ETI EMON config". Lost it? Disconnect the power of the kit, hold button Sw1 and reconnect the power. Then connect to "ETI EMON config": your EMON ID is shown on the screen.

errors.invalid_format: An EMON ID has 12 characters (digits 0–9 and letters A–F).
errors.not_found: No data found for this EMON ID. Check the ID; if your meter has only just started sending data, try again later.
errors.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Try again in an hour.
errors.session_expired: The data cannot be reached right now. Try again later.
errors.upstream_unavailable: The data cannot be reached right now. Try again later.
errors.conflict: Someone else has changed this in the meantime. Reload and try again.

live.title: Live
live.offlineTitle: Your meter has not sent data since {{time}}.
live.offlineHelp: Check that the meter kit has power and that your Wi-Fi works. If that does not help, disconnect the power briefly and reconnect it.
live.chartLabel: Chart of the net power over the last 24 hours
live.gasChartLabel: Bar chart of the gas use per hour over the last 24 hours
live.gasHourlyNote: Your meter reports the gas reading once an hour; use shows up an hour later.

history.title: History
history.energyChart: Bar chart of import and export in this period
history.gasChart: Bar chart of the gas use in this period
history.zoomHint: Tap a bar to zoom in.

settings.title: Settings
settings.removeConfirmText: The app forgets your EMON ID and settings on this device. You can enter it again later.
settings.unavailable: Meter information is not available right now.
settings.countersSwappedHelp: The import and export counters of your meter appear to be swapped (possibly a wiring error). The app corrects this automatically.
settings.aboutPartners: Avans Hogeschool and HZ University of Applied Sciences
settings.installUnsupported: Installing as an app works in Chrome, Edge or Safari.
settings.aboutLicense: Open source under the Apache 2.0 license
settings.licensesError: The licenses could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.

install.title: Install as app
install.bannerText: Add Energiemeter to your home screen for quick access.
install.after: Then open Energiemeter from your home screen, just like an app.

ios.1: Tap the Share button: in Safari at the bottom (iPhone) or top (iPad), in Chrome and Edge next to the address bar.
ios.2: Scroll and choose Add to Home Screen.

macos.1: In the menu bar, choose File → Add to Dock.

tariffs.title: Tariffs
tariffs.intro: Enter the tariffs of your energy contract to see your costs. When your tariff changes, add a new period from the start date.
tariffs.compareHelp: Add a second contract, for example a dynamic one, to see what you would have paid with it.
tariffs.nameHelp: For example the name of the supplier and the type of contract.
tariffs.removeCompareText: The comparison contract and its tariff periods are removed. You can bring it back through earlier versions.
tariffs.deleteText: The period from {{date}} is deleted. You can bring it back through earlier versions.
tariffs.restoreText: The tariffs of this version become the current ones. The current tariffs are kept as an earlier version.

errors.conflict: The tariffs were changed elsewhere in the meantime. They have been reloaded; please try again.
errors.rate_limited: You changed the tariffs many times in the past hour. Try again later.

fields.dynamicMarkupPerKwh: Markup on the export price per kWh
fields.name: Name (optional)

tariffs.validFromHelp: The date these tariffs take effect.
tariffs.inclHelp: Incl. energy tax and VAT, as on your annual statement.
tariffs.markupHelp: Your supplier's purchase fee on top of the market price; may be negative.
tariffs.energyTaxHelp: Energy tax; see the Belastingdienst rates or your contract.
tariffs.compensationHelp: What you receive per kWh you export more than you import (until 2026) or per exported kWh (from 2027).
tariffs.feeHelp: Fee your supplier charges per exported kWh; often 0.
tariffs.dynamicMarkupHelp: Correction on the market price for export, excl. VAT; often negative. Empty = 0.
tariffs.supplierHelp: Fixed supplier charge for electricity and gas together, incl. VAT.
tariffs.gridHelp: Grid operator charge for electricity and gas together, incl. VAT.
tariffs.taxReductionHelp: Energy tax reduction, also called heffingskorting; as a positive amount, incl. VAT.
tariffs.statementHint: You find the amounts on your contract or annual statement. Use a comma or a dot as decimal separator.
tariffs.invalidDate: Enter a date that is not in use yet.
tariffs.namePeriodHelp: To recognise this period in the list.
tariffs.compareOffNote: The comparison is off: the tariff periods are kept, but Live and History show no comparison.

costs.title: Costs
costs.estimatedNote: Estimated: meter data is missing; the use is spread over that period.
costs.proRataNote: Fixed costs and tax reduction count pro rata for the part of the day that has passed.
costs.chartLabel: Bar chart of the costs per period, with a line for the comparison contract

basis.last-year: based on the same days last year
basis.mixed: based on last year and the last 30 days

costs.hint: Enter your tariffs to see costs

lunarnewyear.name: Chinese New Year
lunarnewyear.about: The new year of the Chinese lunar calendar, also called the Spring Festival. Families get together, red lanterns and dragons bring luck and there are fireworks; in the Netherlands it is celebrated in the Chinatowns of Amsterdam, Rotterdam and The Hague, among others.

sweater.name: Warme Truiendag
sweater.about: A day of the Dutch Klimaatverbond: turn the heating down one degree and put on a warm sweater. That saves about 6% of heating energy.

valentine.name: Valentine's Day
valentine.about: On 14 February people show each other they care with a card, flowers or a treat. The day is named after Saint Valentine.

carnival.name: Carnival
carnival.about: Mainly in Brabant and Limburg, people celebrate in the days before Ash Wednesday, dressed up or in a boerenkiel (farmer's smock), with parades and music. Then Lent, the Christian time of fasting before Easter, begins.

eidfitr.name: Suikerfeest (Eid al-Fitr)
eidfitr.about: Eid al-Fitr ends the fasting month of Ramadan. Muslims visit family and friends, share sweets and give to those who have less.

holi.name: Holi Phagwa
holi.about: The Hindu spring festival of good winning over evil. The day after the bonfire people throw coloured powder at each other; in the Netherlands it is mainly celebrated by the Surinamese-Hindustani community.

nowruz.name: Nowruz
nowruz.about: New Year at the start of spring, celebrated by Iranian, Afghan and Kurdish Dutch people, among others. The table holds symbols of a new beginning, such as sprouted wheat (sabzeh) and a goldfish.

earthhour.name: Earth Hour
earthhour.about: On the last Saturday of March, people and buildings around the world switch off their lights for an hour, from 20:30 to 21:30, as a sign for the climate.

easter.name: Easter
easter.about: On Good Friday Christians remember the death of Jesus, and at Easter his resurrection. Coloured eggs and the Easter hare stand for new life and spring.

songkran.name: Songkran
songkran.about: The Thai New Year, 13 to 15 April. Water stands for cleansing and a fresh start: people respectfully sprinkle their elders and happily soak each other.

earthday.name: Earth Day
earthday.about: On 22 April people around the world think about caring for the earth: using less energy, wasting less and protecting nature.

kingsday.name: King's Day
kingsday.about: The birthday of King Willem-Alexander on 27 April (or 26 April when the 27th is a Sunday). The Netherlands turns orange, with flea markets, music and Koningsnacht the evening before.

eidadha.name: Offerfeest (Eid al-Adha)
eidadha.about: Eid al-Adha remembers the faith of the prophet Ibrahim. Muslims come together for prayer, visit family and share food with others, including those who have less.

liberation.name: Liberation Day
liberation.about: On 5 May the Netherlands celebrates the end of the German occupation in 1945 and reflects on the value of freedom. The evening before, on 4 May, the dead are remembered.

solstice.name: Longest day
solstice.about: Around 21 June the sun is at its highest and the day is the longest of the year. Solar panels yield the most.

ketikoti.name: Keti Koti
ketikoti.about: On 1 July the abolition of slavery in Suriname and the former Netherlands Antilles in 1863 is commemorated and celebrated. Keti Koti means 'the chains are broken'. Many people wear koto and angisa in colourful fabrics.

pride.name: Pride Amsterdam
pride.about: A week of events for equal rights and acceptance of LGBTIQ+ people, with the Canal Parade on the Amsterdam canals on the first Saturday of August.

halloween.name: Halloween
halloween.about: On 31 October people dress up spookily and put out carved pumpkins with a candle. The festival comes from Ireland and became popular in the Netherlands via America.

diwali.name: Divali
diwali.about: The festival of lights of Hindus, Sikhs and Jains: light wins over darkness. Homes are lit with oil lamps (diyas) and decorated with rangoli; in the Netherlands it is big in the Surinamese-Hindustani community.

stmartin.name: Sint-Maarten
stmartin.about: On the evening of 11 November children go from door to door with home-made lanterns and sing songs for a treat. It remembers Saint Martin, who shared his cloak with a beggar.

loykrathong.name: Loy Krathong
loykrathong.about: A Thai festival of lights at the full moon in November. People float krathongs, little boats of banana leaf with flowers and a candle, to give thanks and let go of worries.

sinterklaas.name: Sinterklaas
sinterklaas.about: In early December Sinterklaas and his helpers (pieten) bring presents, with pakjesavond on 5 December: surprises, poems and pepernoten.

hanukkah.name: Hanukkah
hanukkah.about: The eight-day Jewish festival of lights remembers the rededication of the Temple in Jerusalem. Each evening one more candle is lit in the hanukkiah.

christmas.name: Christmas
christmas.about: At Christmas Christians celebrate the birth of Jesus. For many people a time of being together, lights and a decorated tree.

newyear.name: New Year's Eve
newyear.about: Saying goodbye to the old year and welcoming the new one, with oliebollen, the countdown to midnight and fireworks.

winter.name: Winter
winter.about: The cold months of the year: short days, maybe snow. This is when a home uses the most energy for heating and light.

spring.name: Spring
spring.about: The days get longer, flowers come up and the bees fly again. Solar panels yield more every week.

summer.name: Summer
summer.about: Long, light days: time for ice cream, the beach and sailing. Solar panels yield the most now, often more than the home uses.

autumn.name: Autumn
autumn.about: The leaves change colour and fall, the days get shorter. The heating goes back on.

dryjanuary.name: Dry January
dryjanuary.about: In January many people take part in Dry January (IkPas in the Netherlands): a month without alcohol, to see how it feels.

movember.name: Movember
movember.about: In November men grow a moustache to raise awareness and money for men's health, such as prostate and testicular cancer and mental health.

bulbtime.name: Bulb season
bulbtime.about: From late March to mid-May the bulb fields are in bloom and Keukenhof is open: fields full of tulips, daffodils and hyacinths.

ramadan.name: Ramadan
ramadan.about: The Islamic month of fasting. Muslims do not eat or drink during the day and break the fast together in the evening with iftar. The month ends with Eid al-Fitr.

advent.name: Advent
advent.about: The four weeks before Christmas. In many homes and churches one more candle is lit on the Advent wreath each Sunday.

sinttime.name: Sinterklaas season
sinttime.about: Sinterklaas is in the country! Children put their shoe by the chimney and sing songs, hoping for pepernoten or a small present.

football.name: Football championship
football.about: A European or World Cup football tournament is on. The Netherlands turns orange and watches the matches together.

springbreak.name: Spring half-term
springbreak.about: The February school holiday: for many families time for winter sports or a quiet week.

maybreak.name: May holiday
maybreak.about: A week of school holiday around King's Day and Liberation Day: time to play outside, for example with a kite.

summerbreak.name: Summer holiday
summerbreak.about: The long school holiday. Many people go away; an empty home mainly uses standby power.

autumnbreak.name: Autumn half-term
autumnbreak.about: A week of school holiday in October: on with the wellies and into the woods.

epiphany.name: Epiphany
epiphany.about: On 6 January Christians remember the three wise men who followed the star to the infant Jesus. In some places children go from door to door with a star.

tulipday.name: National Tulip Day
tulipday.about: On the third Saturday of January the tulip season opens with a big picking garden on Dam Square in Amsterdam, where everyone can pick tulips for free.

poetryday.name: Poetry Day
poetryday.about: On the last Thursday of January poems take centre stage: read one, write one or send one to someone.

birdcount.name: Garden Bird Count
birdcount.about: On the last weekend of January tens of thousands of people count the birds in their garden for half an hour, for research by the Dutch bird protection society.

cleanenergyday.name: International Day of Clean Energy
cleanenergyday.about: On 26 January the United Nations calls attention to clean energy for everyone: sun, wind and using it wisely.

candlemas.name: Candlemas
candlemas.about: On 2 February, forty days after Christmas, candles are blessed in church. In Limburg, Brabant and Belgium people eat pancakes.

wetlandsday.name: World Wetlands Day
wetlandsday.about: On 2 February marshes, rivers and wetlands are in the spotlight: they clean water, store CO2 and give room to birds such as the heron.

efficiencyday.name: World Energy Efficiency Day
efficiencyday.about: On 5 March it is all about using energy smarter: the same warmth and light with fewer kilowatt-hours.

piday.name: Pi Day
piday.about: On 14 March (3/14) maths lovers celebrate the number pi, 3.14159…, preferably with a pie.

womensday.name: International Women's Day
womensday.about: On 8 March we celebrate what women have achieved and call for equal rights. Purple and mimosa yellow are the colours of the day.

booksweek.name: Book Week
booksweek.about: In March bookshops and libraries celebrate books. Buy a book and you get the Book Week gift.

cleanupday.name: National Clean-up Day
cleanupday.about: On a Saturday in March tens of thousands of volunteers pick up litter in their neighbourhood.

treeday.name: Tree Day
treeday.about: On the third Wednesday of March schoolchildren all over the Netherlands plant trees.

waterday.name: World Water Day
waterday.about: On 22 March the United Nations calls attention to clean drinking water, which millions of people still cannot take for granted.

clockchange.name: Clocks change
clockchange.about: On the night of the last Saturday to Sunday of March the clocks go forward an hour (summer time); in October they go back an hour (winter time).

aprilfools.name: April Fools' Day
aprilfools.about: The day of pranks: don't believe everything you hear today. Even our logo acts up now and then.

passover.name: Passover
passover.about: The Jewish festival of Passover remembers the exodus from Egypt. For eight days Jews eat matzah, unleavened bread, and the first evenings have the seder meal.

healthday.name: World Health Day
healthday.about: On 7 April, the founding day of the World Health Organization, the focus is on health for everyone.

artday.name: World Art Day
artday.about: On 15 April, Leonardo da Vinci's birthday, we celebrate art and creativity.

bookday.name: World Book Day
bookday.about: On 23 April we celebrate books and reading, on the day Shakespeare and Cervantes died.

kingsgames.name: King's Games
kingsgames.about: On the Friday before King's Day primary schools start with a shared breakfast and then play sports and games, dressed in orange.

sunday.name: International Sun Day
sunday.about: On 3 May the sun as a source of energy is in the spotlight. A few solar panels on the roof supply a good share of a household's electricity.

europeday.name: Europe Day
europeday.about: On 9 May we celebrate cooperation in Europe, on the anniversary of the 1950 Schuman Declaration.

nursesday.name: International Nurses Day
nursesday.about: On 12 May, Florence Nightingale's birthday, we thank nurses and carers.

millday.name: National Mill Day
millday.about: On the second Saturday of May many of the more than 1,200 Dutch windmills turn and you can often go inside. We have been harvesting wind energy for centuries.

mothersday.name: Mother's Day
mothersday.about: On the second Sunday of May we treat mothers to flowers, breakfast in bed or a home-made present.

ascension.name: Ascension Day
ascension.about: Forty days after Easter Christians remember the ascension of Jesus. For many people a day off, sometimes with a long weekend.

idahot.name: IDAHOBIT
idahot.about: On 17 May it is the International Day against Homophobia, Biphobia and Transphobia: for acceptance and equal rights.

museumday.name: International Museum Day
museumday.about: On 18 May museums around the world celebrate their role for art, culture and history, often with special activities.

beeday.name: World Bee Day
beeday.about: On 20 May bees and other pollinators are in the spotlight: without them there would be no fruit and far fewer flowers.

biodiversityday.name: Biodiversity Day
biodiversityday.about: On 22 May we celebrate the richness of plants and animals, from ladybird to butterfly, and how we protect it.

towelday.name: Towel Day
towelday.about: On 25 May fans of Douglas Adams' 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy' carry a towel. The answer to everything? 42.

vesak.name: Vesak
vesak.about: At the full moon in May Buddhists celebrate the birth, enlightenment and passing of the Buddha, with lights and lotus flowers.

pentecost.name: Pentecost
pentecost.about: Fifty days after Easter Christians celebrate the coming of the Holy Spirit, often shown as a dove or flames. Whit Monday is a day off.

childrensday.name: International Children's Day
childrensday.about: On 1 June children and their rights are in the spotlight; in many countries it is a holiday.

oceansday.name: World Oceans Day
oceansday.about: On 8 June the United Nations calls attention to the oceans, which provide a large part of our oxygen.

flagday.name: Flag Day (Vlaggetjesdag)
flagday.about: In June Scheveningen opens the herring season: the boats are decked with flags and the first Hollandse Nieuwe herring is tasted.

windday.name: Global Wind Day
windday.about: On 15 June wind energy is in the spotlight. A modern onshore wind turbine supplies electricity for a few thousand households.

picnicday.name: International Picnic Day
picnicday.about: On 18 June: pack a basket, bring a blanket and eat outside.

refugeeday.name: World Refugee Day
refugeeday.about: On 20 June we reflect on the millions of people who had to flee their homes. The butterfly stands for the freedom to move.

fathersday.name: Father's Day
fathersday.about: On the third Sunday of June we treat fathers, with a cup of coffee, a drawing or a tie.

emojiday.name: World Emoji Day
emojiday.about: On 17 July, the date shown on the calendar emoji, we celebrate the little pictures we send every day.

fourdays.name: Nijmegen Four Days Marches
fourdays.about: In the third week of July tens of thousands of walkers cover 30 to 50 kilometres a day for four days around Nijmegen, cheered on by crowds. At the end: a medal and gladioli.

friendshipday.name: International Day of Friendship
friendshipday.about: On 30 July we celebrate friendship between people, countries and cultures.

perseids.name: Perseids
perseids.about: Mid-August is the best time for shooting stars: the earth passes through the dust of a comet. Find a dark spot and look up.

schoolstart.name: Back to school
schoolstart.about: In early September schools open again: new class, new teacher, new pencils.

evday.name: World EV Day
evday.about: On 9 September electric vehicles are in the spotlight. Charging an EV with your own solar power is the cheapest and cleanest kilometre.

programmersday.name: Day of the Programmer
programmersday.about: On the 256th day of the year (2⁸) we thank programmers, including those of this app.

monumentday.name: Heritage Days
monumentday.about: On the second weekend of September thousands of monuments open their doors for free: windmills, churches, castles and factories.

roshhashanah.name: Rosh Hashanah
roshhashanah.about: The Jewish New Year. The shofar, a ram's horn, is blown and people eat apple with honey for a sweet new year.

prinsjesdag.name: Prinsjesdag
prinsjesdag.about: On the third Tuesday of September the King rides in his coach to the Hall of Knights for the speech from the throne, and the finance minister presents the budget in the briefcase.

peaceweek.name: Peace Week
peaceweek.about: Around 21 September, the International Day of Peace, PAX organises events for peace all over the Netherlands.

midautumn.name: Mid-Autumn Festival
midautumn.about: The Chinese moon festival at the full moon in September or October: families get together, there are lanterns and everyone eats mooncakes.

neighboursday.name: Neighbours' Day
neighboursday.about: On the fourth Saturday of September neighbours do something fun or useful together for their street.

languagesday.name: European Day of Languages
languagesday.about: On 26 September we celebrate the many languages of Europe. Hallo, hello, salam, hola!

tourismday.name: World Tourism Day
tourismday.about: On 27 September travel is in the spotlight, and how to do it sustainably.

heartday.name: World Heart Day
heartday.about: On 29 September we call attention to a healthy heart: exercise, healthy food and not smoking.

eldersday.name: International Day of Older Persons
eldersday.about: On 1 October we put older people in the spotlight, with a visit, a cup of tea or a chat.

childrensbookweek.name: Children's Book Week
childrensbookweek.about: In October children's books take centre stage for twelve days, at school, in the library and in bookshops.

animalday.name: World Animal Day
animalday.about: On 4 October we spoil our pets and think about the welfare of all animals.

teachersday.name: World Teachers' Day
teachersday.about: On 5 October we thank teachers for everything they teach us.

hydrogenday.name: Hydrogen Day
hydrogenday.about: On 8 October (1.008 is the atomic weight of hydrogen) the focus is on hydrogen as a way to store renewable energy.

sustainabilityday.name: Sustainability Day
sustainabilityday.about: On 10 October people all over the Netherlands show what they do for a more sustainable world, for example with solar panels or a more efficient home.

foodday.name: World Food Day
foodday.about: On 16 October food is in the spotlight: enough healthy food for everyone, and less waste.

nightofthenight.name: Night of the Night
nightofthenight.about: On the last Saturday of October the lights go out in many places, so you can see the stars again and nocturnal animals get some peace.

natureday.name: Nature Work Day
natureday.about: On the first Saturday of November thousands of volunteers spend a day working in nature: pruning, planting and tidying.

glow.name: GLOW Eindhoven
glow.about: For eight evenings in November Eindhoven turns into a light festival with works of art made of light.

carersday.name: Carers' Day
carersday.about: On 10 November we thank the people who care for a loved one who is ill or needs help.

elevenelven.name: The eleventh of the eleventh
elevenelven.about: On 11 November at 11:11 the carnival season starts in the south of the Netherlands, with the announcement of the new carnival prince.

arrival.name: Sinterklaas arrives
arrival.about: In mid-November Sinterklaas arrives in the Netherlands by steamboat, live on television. After that children may put out their shoe.

volunteersday.name: Volunteers' Day
volunteersday.about: On 7 December we thank the millions of volunteers who help others.

purplefriday.name: Purple Friday
purplefriday.about: On the second Friday of December pupils and teachers wear purple to show that everyone at school can be themselves, including LGBTIQ+ young people.

shortestday.name: Shortest day
shortestday.about: Around 21 December the sun is at its lowest and the day is the shortest. Solar panels yield the least now; from tomorrow the days get longer again.

bikeday.name: World Bicycle Day
bikeday.about: On 3 June we celebrate the bicycle: healthy, clean, and in the Netherlands there are more bikes than people.

environmentday.name: World Environment Day
environmentday.about: On 5 June the United Nations calls attention to protecting the environment, from clean air to butterflies along the roadside.

gas.title: Gas analysis
gas.pending: Weather data for station {{name}} is being fetched. The analysis completes by itself.
gas.unavailable: The gas analysis is not available right now. Please try again later.
gas.perDdHint: Heating gas (without base load) divided by degree days. Lower is more efficient; periods with few degree days (summer) are not shown.
gas.lineChart: Gas per day against degree days
gas.lineHint: Each degree day costs {{slope}} m³; without heating demand {{base}} m³ per day. Based on {{days}} heating days of the past year (R² {{r2}}). Grey dots are earlier heating seasons.
gas.lineTooFew: Not enough heating days yet for a heating line.
gas.yearsHint: Actual = measured use on the measured days. Degree days = the whole year. Corrected = use converted to a full year of normal weather ({{normal}} degree days, mean of {{years}} years). Base = automatic or manual base load. CBS median = the temperature-corrected annual use of the middle home with your home profile.
gas.curveChart: Gas per hour against outdoor temperature
gas.profileChart: Average gas use per hour of the day
gas.hourlyShifted: Your meter reports gas once an hour; use is attributed to the hour before.
gas.ownReference: Your use over the past 365 days, converted to a normal weather year: {{m3}} m³.
gas.ownUnknown: Your place in the comparison needs at least 180 measured days in the past year, enough of them in the heating season. The comparison is updated every night.
gas.compareAll: All households with a meter kit
gas.comparePercentile: You use less than {{share}}% of these {{count}} households.
gas.compareTooFew: There are not enough households for a comparison yet.
gas.groupTooSmall: Fewer than 5 similar homes share their profile so far.
gas.cbsMean: Mean {{mean}} m³, median {{median}} m³ per year.
gas.cbsPerM2: Per m² of floor area: you {{own}} m³, CBS median {{median}} m³.
gas.cbsNote: CBS corrects with its own method (KEV, De Bilt), so this comparison is indicative.
gas.hybridNote: CBS only has figures for homes heated with gas; with a hybrid heat pump you naturally use less.
gas.bandLabel: Distribution with median {{median}}; the dot is you
gas.attribution: Weather data: KNMI · Comparison: CBS StatLine 85140NED (CC BY 4.0)
gas.postcodeHelp: Only the first two digits are used: for the nearest KNMI station and, on the server, to compare your use with the weather in your own region.

methodHelp.plain: Base temperature minus the mean outdoor temperature, per day.
methodHelp.weighted: Like plain, with seasonal weighting: Apr–Sep × 0.8, Mar and Oct × 1.0, Nov–Feb × 1.1 (as on mindergas.nl).
methodHelp.effective: Weighted, and wind makes it colder: temperature minus wind speed divided by 1.5.

gas.cooking: Cooking and/or hot water on gas
gas.cookingHelp: A base load is then subtracted before the use per degree day is computed.
gas.baselineHelp: Leave empty for automatic: the median of warm days, without days with no gas use (away).
gas.profileHelp: Classes as used by CBS. Used for the comparison with CBS figures; the profile stays on this device unless you share it below.
gas.shareHelp: Your home profile is stored on the server under an encrypted code, not under your EMON ID. You then see how your use compares with homes like yours; others never see your figures. Switching off removes the profile from the server.
gas.shareFailed: Sharing failed. Please try again later.
gas.cbsPerM2Median: Per m² of floor area: CBS median {{median}} m³.
gas.curveHint: Last 90 days: average gas use per hour at each outdoor temperature.
gas.profileHint: Last 90 days: average gas use per hour of the day, on cold and on mild days.

divisionHelp.calendar: Years from 1 January to 31 December. Only calendar years have the CBS median per year.
divisionHelp.contract: Years from the start date of your energy contract, as on your annual statement.
divisionHelp.heating: Heating seasons from 1 July to 30 June, so a winter is not cut in two.

gas.contractStartTariffs: Leave empty: {{date}}, the start of your gas tariff under Tariffs.
gas.contractStartNone: No gas tariff under Tariffs yet: empty means 1 January.
gas.expectedHelp: On your contract or annual statement; your advance payment is based on it. Used for the settlement forecast.
gas.settlementLess: forecast {{forecast}} of {{expected}} m³ ({{change}}), less than expected
gas.settlementMore: forecast {{forecast}} of {{expected}} m³ ({{change}}), more than expected
gas.settlementNote: Forecast in m³ against your expected annual use; the settlement also depends on prices, fixed costs and the reduction of energy tax.
gas.fillExpected: Fill in your expected annual use for a settlement forecast
